items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: I know that Eddie told me that... Eddie was quite familiar with Pettis, although I think he told me that the most important guy for him early was George Johnson on the Wolverines, a greatly underestimated guy...

ctx.x: It, uh, seems that music was changing rapidly enough that, uh, if you couldn't change with it, it might be left behind. Frankie Quartell says that he dropped out of music. He just couldn't keep up. And, uh, you would recognize him, of course, as an earlier generation, five or ten years of Columbia. And, and he never could quite, uh, rid himself of what was back up. Frank Snyder, uh, as a drummer, too, might have grown out of date. Well, now, uh, the new fellows coming up in Chicago, uh, those who, uh, grew to…

No, they didn't. They had a condom. No, that's a, that's a, a funny thing. There, there are, of course, there are the old legends about what happened when the, when the necessity for learning to read came up. Uh, Paul Mayers, for instance, said any time he had to read what somebody else wrote for him, he'd quit. He said that's why he started the barbecue place on North State. Um, I can remember that, I think it was George Johnson and the Wolverines, when Dick Voino announced that everybody was going to have to…
It was too progressive to have understood it.
